title: Flash Flood Dynamics in Urbanized Campus Terrain
question:
During torrential afternoon downpours, low-lying campus access points like PJ Gate
experience rapid surface waterlogging primarily because:

options.text: Soil absorption suddenly halts completely
High surface runoff exceeds drainage capacity
Atmospheric pressure forces water upward
Underground pipes reverse direction instantly

explanation:
Impervious urban surfaces (asphalt roads, paved car parks) prevent natural infiltration, causing
precipitation volume to rapidly exceed storm drainage discharge thresholds (NADMA, 2023).

title: Safe Pedestrian Protocol for Standing Water
question:
When walking between residential colleges, what is the critical threshold at which moving
water can knock down an adult?

options.text: 15 cm (6 inches) of moving water
45 cm (18 inches) of moving water
60 cm (24 inches) of moving water
Water level must reach waist height

explanation:
As little as 15 cm of moving floodwater exerts substantial lateral kinetic force capable of sweeping an
adult off their feet, concealing open drains and missing manhole covers (FEMA / Ready.gov, 2022).

title: Official Early Warning Interpretations
question:
When MET Malaysia issues an 'Orange' (Severe) Continuous Rain Warning, what does it
signify for the Klang Valley?

options.text: Light drizzle anticipated intermittently
Unprecedented monsoon flooding guaranteed
Continuous rain expected with ≥60mm in 6 hrs
Immediate campus evacuation order

explanation:
An Orange Continuous Rain Warning indicates heavy rainfall exceeding 60 mm within a 6-hour window,
requiring proactive safety precautions and trip rescheduling (MET Malaysia, 2024).

title: Heat Index & Relative Humidity Effects
question:
Why does an ambient temperature of 33°C in Kuala Lumpur feel significantly more
oppressive than the same temperature in a dry climate?

options.text: Solar UV radiation is doubled in tropical zones

High humidity impedes sweat evaporative
cooling
Tropical air contains less breathable oxygen
Higher air density traps solar heat near the skin

explanation:
High atmospheric relative humidity suppresses sweat vaporization—the human body's primary
thermoregulatory cooling mechanism—elevating physiological strain (MOH Malaysia, 2023).

title: Clinical Discrimination: Heat Exhaustion vs. Heat Stroke
question:
Which of the following symptoms distinguishes a life-threatening Heat Stroke from Heat
Exhaustion during outdoor campus transit?

options.text: Heavy perspiration and clammy skin

Altered mental state / confusion and hot, dry
skin
Mild muscle cramping in legs
Dizziness alleviated by seated rest

explanation:
Heat stroke causes core body temperature to surge (>40°C), triggering nervous system dysfunction
(confusion, ataxia, seizures) and cessation of sweating, demanding immediate medical resuscitation (WHO, 2023).

title: Urban Heat Island (UHI) Mitigation on Campus
question:
To minimize personal heat strain when walking between residential colleges and
faculties during peak midday hours, students should:

options.text:
Increase walking pace to minimize total outdoor
time

Utilize continuous tree-canopied corridors and
hydrate
Drink cold iced beverages with high sugar content
Wear tightly woven dark clothing to reflect radiation

explanation:
Shaded green canopy paths reduce radiant surface exposure by up to 10–15°C compared to open
asphalt surfaces, preserving body hydration (IPCC AR6 WGII, 2022).

title: Primary Aerosol Threat in Transboundary Haze
question:
What pollutant in regional biomass haze is considered the greatest hazard to human
respiratory and cardiovascular health?

options.text: Ground-level sulfur hexafluoride (SF6)
Coarse dust particulate matter (>10 µm)
Fine Particulate Matter ≤ 2.5 µm (PM2.5)
Atmospheric nitrogen gas (N2)

explanation:
PM2.5 particles penetrate deeply into lung alveoli and cross into the bloodstream, triggering systemic
inflammatory and cardiovascular events (Department of Environment Malaysia, 2023).

title: Malaysia Air Pollutant Index (API) Thresholds
question:
According to the APIMS standard, an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading between 101 and
200 is classified as:

options.text: Moderate (Standard outdoor activity permitted)

Unhealthy (Sensitive groups should restrict
outdoor exposure)

Very Unhealthy (All vigorous outdoor activity
ceased)
Hazardous (Immediate lockdown of public areas)

explanation:
API 101–200 signifies the 'Unhealthy' band where people with respiratory ailments experience
worsening symptoms and the general public should limit prolonged physical exertion outdoors (Department of
Environment Malaysia, 2023).

title: Effective Respiratory Protection Standards
question:
When walking outdoors during an Unhealthy haze event (API 150+), which protective face
covering is certified to filter PM2.5?

options.text: Standard 3-ply surgical mask
Washable single-layer cotton bandana

Well-fitted particulate respirator (N95 / KF94 /
KN95)
Double-layered silk gaiter

explanation:
Surgical and cloth masks allow fine sub-micron particulates to leak around loose edges. Particulate
respirators (N95/KF94) provide sealed electrostatic filtration against PM2.5 (MOH Malaysia, 2023).

title: Vehicle Hydroplaning & Submergence Risks
question:
When driving or commuting across campus during a flash flood, what depth of flowing
water can float or carry away most passenger cars?

options.text: 10 cm (4 inches)
30 cm (12 inches)
75 cm (30 inches)
Water must submerge the vehicle hood

explanation:
Approximately 30 cm (1 foot) of moving water exerts sufficient buoyant force to lift and displace most
light passenger vehicles and subcompact cars (FEMA / Ready.gov, 2022).

title: Electrical Hazards Post-Flood Event
question:
After a severe storm recedes near faculty basements, what immediate secondary hazard
should students avoid?

options.text:
Submerged electrical conduits, junction boxes,
and fallen wires
Sudden decreases in outdoor air pressure
Rapid depletion of local ground nitrogen
Elevated ozone concentrations in soil puddles

explanation:
Floodwaters conduct electric currents from damaged feeder pillars and low-voltage substations,
creating fatal electrocution hazards without visible sparks (NADMA, 2023).

title: Early Warning Color Coding Hierarchy
question:
Under MET Malaysia's continuous rain advisory system, a 'Red' (Danger) Warning
explicitly alerts the community that:

options.text: Light drizzle will persist for over 48 hours

A tropical cyclone has formed directly over Kuala
Lumpur

Continuous heavy rain exceeding 240mm in 24
hrs is imminent
Academic activities are permanently shifted online

explanation:
The Red warning is MET Malaysia's highest alert tier, denoting rainfall accumulation projected to
exceed 240 mm within 24 hours (MET Malaysia, 2024).

title: First Response for Severe Heat Stress
question:
If a peer collapses during outdoor sports on campus displaying hot, dry skin and delirium,
your immediate first-aid priority while calling emergency services is:

options.text: Force-feed large volumes of electrolyte liquid

Move them to shade and initiate active cooling
with cold water/ice packs
Cover them with an emergency thermal foil blanket
Administer oral paracetamol or aspirin

explanation:
Unconscious or delirious individuals must never be forced to drink due to aspiration risks. Immediate
passive and active evaporative cooling (ice on groin/neck/axilla) halts fatal brain cell necrosis (WHO, 2023).

title: Hydration Physiology & Diuretics
question:
Why should students avoid relying on heavily caffeinated energy drinks to combat
afternoon fatigue during heatwaves?

options.text: Caffeine permanently stops internal body sweating

High caffeine has mild diuretic effects and
elevates metabolic rate
Caffeine prevents cellular uptake of glucose

Energy drinks destroy salt balances in the stomach
lining

explanation:
Excessive caffeine accelerates fluid loss through mild diuresis while raising cardiac workload and
internal thermal load, compounding dehydration (MOH Malaysia, 2023).

title: Vulnerable Populations & Acclimatization
question:
How long does physiological heat acclimatization typically take for incoming students
newly arriving to a hot, humid tropical environment?

options.text: 24 to 48 hours
10 to 14 days of gradual daily outdoor exposure
Exactly 6 months
Tropical acclimatization is biologically impossible

explanation:
Full circulatory and thermoregulatory adaptation (lower heart rate, increased sweat efficiency,
expanded plasma volume) requires approximately 10 to 14 days of progressive exposure (WHO, 2023).

title: Indoor Air Quality Management During High API
question:
To maintain safe indoor air quality in residential college rooms during severe
transboundary haze, residents should:

options.text:
Keep all windows wide open to circulate natural
outdoor breezes

Keep windows and doors tightly sealed and set
air conditioning to internal recirculate

Burn scented candles to deodorize smoky air
particles
Use standard ceiling fans with open balcony doors

explanation:
Closing building apertures and recirculating internal cooled air prevents exterior particulate ingress.
Burning incense or candles introduces additional dangerous volatile organic compounds (Department of
Environment Malaysia, 2023).

title: Meteorological Influence on Haze Dispersion
question:
Which seasonal meteorological phenomenon is predominantly responsible for
transporting regional biomass haze towards Peninsular Malaysia?

options.text: Northeast Monsoon (NEM) cold surge winds
Southwest Monsoon (SWM) prevailing winds
Inter-monsoon localized convective storms
Polar vortex displacement winds

explanation:
The Southwest Monsoon (typically June to September) creates dry atmospheric conditions and steady
south-westerly winds that carry smoke plumes across the Strait of Malacca (MET Malaysia, 2024).

title: High-Risk Student Demographics
question:
When the campus API crosses 150 (Unhealthy), which student sub-population requires
priority physical activity restriction?

options.text:
Individuals with pre-existing asthma, chronic
bronchitis, or cardiovascular disease
Students with contact lenses only
Only varsity athletes undergoing competitive trials
Only students living in ground-floor dormitories

explanation:
Microscopic aerosols irritate hyperreactive bronchial pathways, triggering severe bronchospasms and
acute exacerbations in asthmatic individuals (MOH Malaysia, 2023).
